issues.legal_issue: The absence of a prior demand to surrender possession does not by itself invalidate an actual forcible dispossession for the purposes of the repeal saving where the dispossessed person does not challenge the dispossession within a reasonable time.
material_facts: The State claimed that it had taken physical possession of the surplus land, but the possession certificate recorded a unilateral taking and there was no evidence of notice to the former owner.
The former owner did not complain of the alleged breach during his lifetime; his heirs challenged the taking many years later after the repeal had taken effect.
issues.conclusion: If physical possession was in fact taken, the absence of notice did not by itself vitiate the taking for the purposes of the repeal saving; the failure to raise a timely grievance implied waiver of the right to object to that procedural breach.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999, and 10(5) and 10(6) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, govern the saving of land for which possession was taken and the procedure for taking possession. Section 10(5) provides the ordinary procedure before forcible dispossession under Section 10(6), but a breach does not necessarily nullify an actual taking; it may give rise to a grievance seeking restoration before the authorities take possession again after notice. A grievance must be raised within a reasonable time, or the right may be treated as waived. State of Uttar Pradesh v. Hari Ram, (2013) 4 SCC 280, concerned whether notice was discretionary and did not decide whether breach of Section 10(5) nullified an actual dispossession.

rule.if: repeal_saving_claim and actual_physical_possession_taken and prior_notice_not_given and no_timely_grievance

predicates.repeal_saving_claim: A party relies on a repeal provision that preserves land where the government has taken possession.
predicates.actual_physical_possession_taken: The government or an authorised official in fact takes physical possession of the land.
predicates.prior_notice_not_given: The government or authorised official takes possession without first giving the occupant a demand to surrender it.
predicates.no_timely_grievance: The person dispossessed does not challenge the taking within a reasonable time.

issues.definition: When a party relies on a repeal saving, actual physical possession taken without prior notice remains effective for that saving if the dispossessed person does not raise a timely grievance.

issues.legal_issue: A prior proceeding that upheld vesting or allotment does not establish that physical possession was taken when possession was neither raised nor determined in that proceeding.
material_facts: Purchasers had unsuccessfully challenged the vesting proceedings and allotment of part of the land, including in proceedings that reached the Supreme Court.
The question whether the former owner or purchasers had been physically dispossessed was not raised or determined in those proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal of the purchasers’ challenge and the confirmation of allotments did not support a finding that physical possession had been taken.
issues.legal_principle: A determination in prior litigation cannot establish a factual issue that was not raised or decided there. The Court distinguished State of Gujarat v. Gyanaba Dilavarsinh Jadega, (2013) 11 SCC 486, where the question of possession was remitted for determination; the prior purchaser proceedings in this case had not determined possession.

predicates.prior_proceeding_challenged_vesting_or_a: A previous proceeding challenged the vesting of land or its allotment to others.
predicates.possession_not_litigated_or_decided: The previous proceeding did not raise or determine whether the government had taken physical possession.

issues.definition: A previous proceeding challenging vesting or allotment does not establish physical possession if that proceeding did not decide the possession issue.

issues.legal_issue: A direction to restore land cannot stand on a record that does not determine whether the former owner remained in physical possession, where possession is seriously disputed and no evidence is identified that would enable a satisfactory determination on remand.
material_facts: The State asserted that it had taken possession, while the former owner’s heirs claimed continuing possession.
The High Court’s appellate order did not specifically find that the former owner had remained in possession after vesting and the recorded taking.
The parties relied on competing affidavits, and no documentary evidence was identified that could resolve the possession dispute on remand.
Bills relied on to support continuing possession related only to a later period and did not substantiate the asserted caretaker’s connection to the property.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the direction restoring possession and affirmed the Single Judge’s order; remanding the case to determine possession was not a viable solution on the evidence identified.
issues.legal_principle: The meaning of possession in Section 3 of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999, is actual physical possession, not possession arising merely from statutory vesting. A seriously disputed question of actual possession may not be capable of satisfactory determination in proceedings under Article 226 of the Constitution; remand is not useful where the parties identify no evidence that would enable the determination. The Court referred to State of Gujarat v. Gyanaba Dilavarsinh Jadega, (2013) 11 SCC 486, in which a remand to determine possession had been made, but found remand unviable on this record.

rule.if: appeal_against_writ_restoration_order and actual_possession_seriously_disputed and no_specific_finding_of_continued_possession and no_identified_evidence_for_remand

predicates.appeal_against_writ_restoration_order: An appeal challenges a writ-court direction to restore possession of land.
predicates.actual_possession_seriously_disputed: The parties give conflicting accounts of who physically possessed the land.
predicates.no_specific_finding_of_continued_possess: The order under appeal does not specifically find that the former owner remained in physical possession.
predicates.no_identified_evidence_for_remand: The parties identify no evidence capable of resolving the possession dispute on remand.

issues.definition: In an appeal against a writ-court restoration direction, the direction is set aside when physical possession is seriously disputed, continued possession was not specifically found, and no evidence for resolving the dispute on remand is identified.

issues.legal_issue: Restoration is not a feasible resolution where the disputed land has been allotted to third parties whose allotments are not challenged and who are not parties to the proceeding.
material_facts: The disputed area had been settled in favour of several families and had also been allotted in part to a development authority.
The allotments were not under challenge in the appeals, and the allottees had not been joined as parties.
The heirs proposed restoring only the portion allotted to the development authority, but the State’s affidavit stated that the disputed land had been settled to the allottees.
issues.conclusion: The proposed partial restoration was not a feasible solution, particularly because the allotments were not challenged and the affected allottees were not parties.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to order restoration on the proposed basis because the challenged relief would affect existing allotments that were not themselves in question and the affected allottees had not been impleaded.

rule.if: appeal_against_restoration_order and disputed_land_allotted_to_third_parties and allotments_not_challenged and allottees_not_joined

predicates.appeal_against_restoration_order: An appeal concerns an order directing restoration of disputed land.
predicates.disputed_land_allotted_to_third_parties: The disputed land has been allotted to persons other than the litigants.
predicates.allotments_not_challenged: The validity of those allotments is not challenged in the proceeding.
predicates.allottees_not_joined: The persons holding the allotments are not parties to the proceeding.

issues.definition: A proposed restoration is not feasible in an appeal concerning restoration when the disputed land has been allotted to third parties, the allotments are unchallenged, and the allottees are not parties.
